definition.def: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.
examples: Try to estimate how many steps it will take to get to a close object. [VERB wh]
I estimate that the total cost for treatment will be $12,500. [VERB that]
He estimated the speed of the winds from the degree of damage. [VERB noun]
Some analysts estimate its current popularity at around ten per cent. [VERB noun + at]
His personal riches were estimated at £368 million. [V n at amount]

definition.def: An estimate is an approximate calculation of a quantity or value.
examples: ...the official estimate of the election result. [+ of/for]
This figure is five times the original estimate.
A recent estimate was that factories were undermanned by about 30 per cent.

definition.def: An estimate is a judgment about a person or situation which you make based on the available evidence.
examples: I hadn't been far wrong in my estimate of his grandson's capabilities. [+ of]

definition.def: An estimate from someone who you employ to do a job for you, such as a builder or a plumber, is a written statement of how much the job is likely to cost.
examples: Estimates for curtain-making can be prepared by computer on the spot.
